title: 2025 against target
prompt: `sales_2025` holds 2025's non-cancelled order lines, with `quarter` and `channel` columns, and `targets` is the finance team's wide sheet. Build `grid`, a pivot table of revenue with quarters 1 to 4 as rows and channels as columns. Melt `targets` into `targets_long` with the columns `channel`, `quarter` (an integer 1 to 4) and `target`. Then make `vs_target`: `targets_long` plus a `revenue` column with the actual revenue for each channel and quarter. Finally set `beat` to the number of rows where revenue reached the target.
hints: `targets.melt(id_vars="channel", var_name="quarter", value_name="target")`, then turn `"Q1"` into `1` with `.str[1].astype(int)`.
Aggregate actuals to the same grain with `groupby(["channel", "quarter"], as_index=False)["revenue"].sum()`, merge on both keys, and count `(vs_target["revenue"] >= vs_target["target"]).sum()`.
explanation: The grid is for people; the long table is for computing. Melting the targets and aggregating the actuals to the same grain (one row per channel and quarter) makes the comparison a plain merge on two keys, and `validate="one_to_one"` confirms each target met exactly one actual. Cartwheel hit 8 of 12 targets; all four misses came in the first half of the year, and then it beat Q4 everywhere by a wide margin: web Q4 revenue was 87,530 dollars against a 60,000 target. Another clue that something unusual happened in Q4.

checks.grid: `grid` is 4 quarters × 3 channels, with web Q4 at about 87,530
checks.vs-target: `vs_target` has 12 rows and actual revenue adding up to 2025's total
